features.description:
System health checkup: one read-only command, bin/health, that runs a health script per concern and reports every check as ok or FAIL.

Contract for a concern check: an executable <group>/health in this repo (one level below the root). It prints one line per check on stdout, `ok <check>[: <detail>]` or `FAIL <check>: <detail>`, and exits 0 iff it printed no FAIL line. It only reads machine state; it never writes, and never prints env var or secret values. When a command a check needs is missing from PATH, the check prints `FAIL <check>: <cmd> not found`; when it exits nonzero in a way the check does not expect, `FAIL <check>: <cmd> exited <rc>`.

Acceptance criteria:
1. bin/health finds every executable `*/health` one level below the repo root, except bin/ (bin/health itself). The root defaults to the repo containing bin/health and is overridable with SKOGAI_HEALTH_ROOT. If the root is missing or not a directory, bin/health prints `health: root <path> is not a directory` to stderr and exits 2 without running anything. It runs each script with stdin from /dev/null and stderr suppressed, and prints each check line as `<group> ok|FAIL <check>[: <detail>]`. All groups, including `skogai` (criterion 2), are printed in alphabetical order of group name.
2. bin/health also runs `bin/check-routes <root>` against the same root as group `skogai`, check `routes`: `ok routes` on exit 0, otherwise `FAIL routes: <n> missing`, where n is the count of `MISSING` lines it printed.
3. After the checks it prints `all N checks ok` and exits 0, or `F of N checks failed` and exits 1.
4. A concern script that exits nonzero without printing a FAIL line is reported as `<group> FAIL health: exited <rc>` and counts as one failed check. A script that prints a FAIL line but exits 0 still counts as failed. A script that exits 0 and prints no check lines is reported as `<group> FAIL health: no checks reported`. Lines matching neither form are ignored.
5. A concern script running longer than HEALTH_TIMEOUT seconds (default 120) is killed. Check lines it printed before being killed are still reported and counted, and `<group> FAIL health: timed out after <n>s` is added as one more failed check.
6. containers/health runs quadlet-health, by default $HOME/.config/containers/systemd/bin/quadlet-health, overridable with QUADLET_HEALTH. On exit 0 it prints `ok quadlet-health: <n> units`, n taken from the `generator:` line (`generator: ok, <n> units` or `generator: rc=<rc>, <n> units`). Otherwise `FAIL quadlet-health: exit <rc>, see quadlet-health`. A missing or non-executable script gives `FAIL quadlet-health: <path> not found`.
7. mise/health runs three checks, each with cwd $HOME:
   a. `doctor` runs `mise doctor`. Its output ends with optional blocks like
        1 warning found:
        <blank>
        1. new mise version 2026.11.2 available, currently on 2026.10.17
        <blank>
        1 problem found:
        <blank>
        1. tool aqua:anthropics/claude-code@2.1.318 is not installed, install with `mise install`
      The check fails iff a line matching `^[0-9]+ problems? found:$` exists; the detail is the numbered lines (`^[0-9]+\. `) of that block, without their number prefix, joined with `; `. Warning blocks never fail it. A nonzero exit with no problem block is `FAIL doctor: mise doctor exited <rc>`.
   b. `bootstrap-plan` runs `mise bootstrap plan`. It finds the line matching `^Plan: `, verbatim e.g. `Plan: 0 create, 0 update, 13 unchanged, 0 remove, 0 unknown`. ok with that line as detail iff create, update, remove and unknown are all 0; else FAIL with that line as detail. No `Plan:` line is `FAIL bootstrap-plan: no Plan: line (exit <rc>)`.
   a/c pass line: exactly `ok doctor`, `ok dot-capture`.
   c. `dot-capture` runs `mise dot status`. A nonzero exit is `FAIL dot-capture: mise dot status exited <rc>`. Otherwise ok iff the output has a line starting `Automatic capture` and the next non-blank line starts with `running` (leading whitespace trimmed for both); else `FAIL dot-capture: automatic capture not running`.
8. machine/health has one check, `failed-units`, from `systemctl --user --failed --no-legend --plain`: `ok failed-units` when it lists no units, else `FAIL failed-units: <unit>[, <unit>...]` (first column of each line). A nonzero exit is `FAIL failed-units: systemctl exited <rc>` regardless of output. machine/SKOGAI.md is added as a short router page and routed from SKOGAI.md; check-routes must still pass.
9. tests/health.test.sh covers criteria 1-8 with stub concern scripts in a temp SKOGAI_HEALTH_ROOT and stub `mise`, `systemctl` and quadlet-health on PATH/env; no test depends on live machine state. It runs under full_test.

QA binding: evidence_type unit (tests/health.test.sh).

Out of scope: a timer or notification (later feature), checks for secrets/, shell/, desktop/, agents/ (they join by adding their own health file).
features.coverage: 25/25 cases; every branch of bin/health, containers/health, mise/health, machine/health exercised (no bash coverage tool; cases mapped to criteria 1-8)

features.description:
secrets/health: key and fnox config permissions.

Follows the concern-check contract in F001 (bin/health): prints `ok <check>[: <detail>]` / `FAIL <check>: <detail>` lines, exits 0 iff no FAIL, read-only, never prints env or secret values. A missing command gives `FAIL <check>: <cmd> not found`. Shared helpers may live in tests/lib.sh (test stubs) and bin/health-lib.sh (sourced by concern scripts); bin/health skips bin/ so neither is run as a check. Tests use stubs only (temp HOME, stub commands on a minimal PATH), never live machine state, and run under full_test.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `ssh-dir`: $HOME/.ssh is a directory owned by the current user with mode 700 -> `ok ssh-dir`; missing -> `FAIL ssh-dir: ~/.ssh not found`; else `FAIL ssh-dir: ~/.ssh is <mode> <owner>, want 700 <user>`.
2. `age-keys`: every file matching $HOME/.ssh/*age*.txt is owned by the current user with mode 600 -> `ok age-keys: <n> keys` (n may be 0); else `FAIL age-keys: <file> <mode> <owner>[, ...]` (basenames, sorted).
3. `fnox-config`: FNOX_CONFIG (default /etc/skogai/fnox.toml) absent -> `ok fnox-config: not deployed`. Present: the file must be mode 644 and its directory mode 755, both owned by FNOX_CONFIG_OWNER (default root) -> `ok fnox-config`; else `FAIL fnox-config: <path> is <mode> <owner>[; <dir> is <mode> <owner>], want 644/755 <owner>` listing only what is wrong. The file's contents are never read.
4. tests/health-secrets.test.sh covers 1-3 with a temp HOME and a temp FNOX_CONFIG (owner override = the test user for the ok path).
5. secrets/SKOGAI.md routes `health`; secrets/fnox.md's draft status line is corrected to say /etc/skogai/fnox.toml exists (seen 2026-11-06, owned by skogix).

QA binding: evidence_type unit (tests/health-secrets.test.sh).
F002-F005 are built sequentially by one implementer; each may create or extend tests/lib.sh and bin/health-lib.sh (the stock-reset rule lives in bin/health-lib.sh).
fnox-config FAIL lists only the wrong parts, joined by `; `, then `, want 644/755 <owner>`: e.g. file ok, dir wrong -> `FAIL fnox-config: /etc/skogai is 775 root, want 644/755 root`.

features.description:
shell/health: atuin sync freshness and secret-looking dotfile var names.

Follows the concern-check contract in F001 (bin/health): prints `ok <check>[: <detail>]` / `FAIL <check>: <detail>` lines, exits 0 iff no FAIL, read-only, never prints env or secret values. A missing command gives `FAIL <check>: <cmd> not found`. Shared helpers may live in tests/lib.sh (test stubs) and bin/health-lib.sh (sourced by concern scripts); bin/health skips bin/ so neither is run as a check. Tests use stubs only (temp HOME, stub commands on a minimal PATH), never live machine state, and run under full_test.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `atuin-sync` runs `atuin status`. Verbatim sample line: `Last sync: 2026-11-06 14:57:47.347674749 +01:00:00`. It parses date, time (seconds, fraction dropped) and offset (+HH:MM from +HH:MM:SS). Younger than ATUIN_SYNC_MAX_AGE_HOURS (default 24) -> `ok atuin-sync: <h>h ago`; older -> `FAIL atuin-sync: last sync <h>h ago`; no parseable `Last sync:` line -> `FAIL atuin-sync: no Last sync: line`; nonzero exit -> `FAIL atuin-sync: atuin status exited <rc>`.
2. `atuin-vars` runs `atuin dotfiles var list`. Verbatim line form: `export NAME=value`. Takes NAME only (the text between `export ` and the first `=`); values are discarded before any processing and never printed. A NAME matching (case-insensitive) KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASSWD or CREDENTIAL is secret-looking -> `FAIL atuin-vars: secret-looking names: <A>, <B>` (sorted); else `ok atuin-vars: <n> vars`. Nonzero exit -> `FAIL atuin-vars: atuin dotfiles var list exited <rc>`.
3. Missing atuin -> both checks `FAIL <check>: atuin not found`.
4. tests/health-shell.test.sh covers 1-3 with a stub atuin; a test asserts a stubbed secret value never appears in the output. TZ-independent (stub times are relative to `date`).
5. shell/SKOGAI.md routes `health`.

QA binding: evidence_type unit (tests/health-shell.test.sh).
F002-F005 are built sequentially by one implementer; each may create or extend tests/lib.sh and bin/health-lib.sh (the stock-reset rule lives in bin/health-lib.sh).
atuin-sync: <h> is the age in floored whole hours; ok iff the age in seconds < ATUIN_SYNC_MAX_AGE_HOURS*3600 (exactly at the limit fails). A nonzero exit wins over any parsed line.
atuin-vars: NAME is split on `_`; it is secret-looking iff any part equals (case-insensitive) one of the words. So TERMIX_TAILSCALE_API_KEY is flagged, KEYMAP and MONKEY are not.

features.description:
bin/health on a timer with a desktop notification on failure, the quadlet-health pattern.

Acceptance criteria:
1. machine/units/skogai-health.service: Type=oneshot, ExecStart=%h/.config/skogai/bin/health, OnFailure=skogai-health-notify.service, Environment=PATH with %h/.local/share/mise/shims first then /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin (so mise, atuin, herdr, jq resolve under the user manager).
2. machine/units/skogai-health-notify.service: Type=oneshot, ExecStart=/usr/bin/notify-send -u critical -a skogai-health "skogai-health failed" "journalctl --user -u skogai-health -n 50".
3. machine/units/skogai-health.timer: OnStartupSec=10min, OnUnitActiveSec=1h, [Install] WantedBy=timers.target.
4. tests/health-units.test.sh asserts those lines and, when systemd-analyze is available, that `systemd-analyze --user verify` accepts the three files (skip, not fail, when it is absent).
5. machine/SKOGAI.md documents install (`systemctl --user link` each unit, `systemctl --user enable --now skogai-health.timer`) as a manual step skogix confirms; this feature does not install or enable anything.

features.description:
bin/check-coverage: every entry in ~/.config is tracked by mise dotfiles or has a written decision.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Entries = every directory and regular file directly in CONFIG_DIR (default $HOME/.config), skipping names starting with `.` and names matching `*.bak` or `*.bak.*`.
2. Tracked = entries whose name equals the first path segment after `~/.config/` of any `.entries[].path` in `mise dot paths --json` (run with cwd $HOME; jq parses it). So `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` tracks `herdr`.
3. Decided = rows of the table in mise/coverage.md (path overridable with COVERAGE_FILE): `| <name> | exclude|owner | <why> |`; other rows and text are ignored. A name with a decision that is also tracked is reported as `CONFLICT <name>: tracked and <decision>` and fails.
4. Output: one `UNDECIDED <name>` line per entry neither tracked nor decided (sorted), then `<t> tracked, <d> decided, <u> undecided` . Exit 0 iff no UNDECIDED and no CONFLICT, 1 otherwise, 2 if `mise dot paths --json` fails or jq/mise is missing (message on stderr).
5. mise/coverage.md explains the three outcomes and is seeded only with decisions skogix already made in PROJECT.md section 2 ("app profiles, caches, logins (never track)") for entries that exist on this machine; nothing else is decided by the agent.
6. Not part of bin/health (it would fail until section 2 is worked through). Routed from mise/SKOGAI.md and the root SKOGAI.md.
7. tests/check-coverage.test.sh covers 1-4 with a temp CONFIG_DIR, a stub mise and a temp COVERAGE_FILE.

QA binding: evidence_type unit (tests/check-coverage.test.sh).
Clarifications: entries include symlinks that resolve to a directory or regular file (dangling links are skipped). Sorting is bytewise (LC_ALL=C). Output order: CONFLICT lines (sorted), then UNDECIDED lines (sorted), then the summary `<t> tracked, <d> decided, <u> undecided, <c> conflicts`. A CONFLICT entry counts only in c. t and d count only entries that exist in CONFIG_DIR. Only `.entries[]` with `mode == "track"` count as tracked (verified 2026-11-06: excludes live in a separate top-level `exclude` key; all 54 entries are track). Entry paths may start with `~/.config/` or `$HOME/.config/`; both are handled.
Seed: only entries PROJECT.md section 2 names explicitly and that exist on this machine, each with decision `owner` (app profiles, caches and logins belong to their app). "chrome variants" and "..." stay undecided.
